cells.tense: You are collecting your own thinking and it is landing where it should — between people.
cells.ask: Say out loud what you decided about someone you have been quietly carrying, and let them hear the whole version.
cells.core:
You are gathering what got scattered and putting it back in one piece. Nothing showy in it — you pick up a loose end of thinking, look at it, find where it belongs. What you decide that way turns out to be right about people, which you know by how easily they settle once you have spoken.

Because your thinking runs clean, peace between you and the people close to you does too. Nothing is being weighed in secret. That is the sort of fairness that does not need to calculate itself. So tell one person what you already worked out, the whole of it, and let the plain truth of it sit in the room between you.
cells.sheetLine: You gather your thinking and it lands right between people.
cells.verb: gathering scattered lines of thought back into one
cells.place: where two people are moving back toward each other

cells.tense: You will have squared every account before anyone has had a chance to say a word.
cells.ask: Let one thing that is not yours to settle stay where it is, and do something with your hands instead.
cells.core:
When your thinking moves at the right pace, you collect the loose ends, set them down in one place, and stop there. The other person gets room to arrive at their own speed and the middle holds without you holding it. What you bring to the table is clear, and you leave it there for them to pick up.

What is happening now is the collecting running ahead of the room. You are trying to have the whole thing finished before it starts — every account squared, every hurt already answered, each part resolved in your head before a word has been said. Pick one tangle that is not yours and leave it where it is. Give your hands a simple task while it settles.
cells.sheetLine: You are settling what is not yours before anyone speaks.

cells.tense: You gave up trying to collect your thinking about them a long time ago.
cells.ask: Tell one person one true thing about what happened, in a sentence, and do not wait to feel like saying it.
cells.core:
When this is moving, feeling and words sit close together. Something registers in the chest and a sentence for it arrives soon after, so the person across from you gets to meet the real version. That exchange is what the connection is for.

What is left here is the feeling without the sentence. You can still sense what you hold about someone, plain as anything, and the words for it have not gotten assembled. So nothing gets said, and the other person keeps talking to a careful version. Sit with that person in your mind a while. Let the feeling settle, then say one true sentence out loud to somebody.
cells.sheetLine: The feeling is still there. The sentence never got built.

cells.tense: You are already the thing holding people together, while calling it nothing much.
cells.ask: Tell someone a story about a time your family got through something, and say why you keep telling it.
cells.core:
You notice who needs asking, which two need a word in the right ear, where the shapes have to shift so a table works. And you do it from your own judgment, knowing it is your judgment, so what you hand over arrives with you in it.

That work is already happening. It gets filed under just being practical, and people leave your table steadier than they arrived because of what you did. The care is not invisible to them; it is invisible to you. Tell one of them a story about the time your lot got through something, and say why it is still worth telling.

attempts.check: The record does not say this person gathers thoughts in order to make peace between people — the card is mental integration, and the seat is connection, so I am joining two facts the record keeps apart. A reader could reasonably say the gathering has nothing to do with anyone else, and that only their own head is involved. The asks all work whichever way it is: telling someone what you decided, listening before you agree, or saying the plain thing to one person pays off whether the reunion was private or between people. The sentence that serves the writer is any version of 'two people moving back toward the middle', which sounds like a wedding toast and says nothing about the work of collecting lines of thought.
